articles.title: The $849 ABS Cyclone RTX 5060 Gaming PC Is More Powerful AND Less Expensive Than the Steam Machine
articles.summary: Shopping around for a budget PC under $1,000? For a limited time, Walmart is offering the ABS Cyclone Aqua gaming PC with GeForce RTX 5060 graphics card for just $849 shipped.
body: The ABS Cyclone gaming PC is equipped with an Intel Core 5 Processor 120, GeForce RTX 5060 GPU, 16GB of DDR4 RAM, and a 1TB NVMe SSD. The Intel Core 5 120 CPU is a 6-core, 12-thread processor with a max boost clock of 4.5GHz. Note that this sytem uses DDR4 instead of DDR5 memory. You won't notice any performance difference during gaming, but keep in mind that you'll need to upgrade both the motherboard and processor if you ever want to move to DDR5 RAM.

The RTX 5060 outperforms its predecessor the RTX 4060 by about 20%-30% and that's before factoring in DLSS 4 with multi-frame generation. This is a solid budget option for 1080p gaming and you should be able to squeeze consistent 60fps+ framerate out of just about any game. If you're gunning for higher resolutions like 1440p or 4K, however, you'll definitely want to upgrade to an RTX 5060 Ti (16GB) or better.

articles.title: Obsession Star Inde Navarrette Says She Studied Anime Like Jujutsu Kaisen and Demon Slayer to Learn Screenwriting
articles.summary: Inde Navarrette, best known for her role as Nikki Freeman in Obsession, says she took a deep dive into anime to better understand screenwriting and storytelling while waiting for her star to rise. Navarrette’s breakout role as Nikki in Obsession didn’t skyrocket her to stardom overnight.
body: During that period, she began to stream games on Twitch to make ends meet, and even started studying storytelling in film and TV by watching some of her favorite anime series — specifically, Demon Slayer and Jujutsu Kaisen.

“I transitioned into studying film and watching movies and asking, ‘Why do I like them?’” she said in an October 14 interview with The Hollywood Reporter. “What I like is anime, so like, why do I like that? I mean, Jujutsu Kaisen I find to be a very fascinating anime, but why is it so different than Demon Slayer? Why is it so different than other ones? With Jujutsu Kaisen, they play with timelines, right? With Demon Slayer, they don’t, it’s very linear. And what does that mean and how does that affect with storytelling?

“I really dove into, ‘Why is Jujutsu Kaisen so good?’ And I learned about timeline and about storytelling — how a person can have a monologue at the beginning of the episode that matters two episodes later or even at the end, and that person’s dead and you don’t learn it until then — and then attaching that to my screenwriting and trying to learn that way.”

articles.title: The 10 Most Underrated RPGs of the Last Decade, Ranked
articles.summary: There’s something about the RPG genre. These games tell amazing stories players want to experience time and time again, are populated by memorable characters, and often explore deep themes — even if their heroes do tend to have memory problems, spiky hair, and swords the size of New Jersey.
body: A truly great RPG is a generational treat. Players flock to the newest Final Fantasy, or to acclaimed newcomers like Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 and Metaphor: ReFantazio. But there have been plenty of other great games released over the last ten years or so, and they didn’t always receive the attention they should have. Here is our list of 10 of the most underrated RPGs of the last decade, ready to point you toward some of the very best experiences you may have missed.

If you can appreciate 16-bit visuals, CrossCode is the action-RPG for you. Set in the far-flung future, it features brisk combat, challenging puzzles, and a unique sci-fi story to tie it all together. As sometimes happens in classic RPGs, the hero wakes with no memory and is also unable to speak. The game’s design was influenced by a number of classic RPGs from the era it mimics, including the likes of Chrono Trigger and even Terranigma (which will get an unexpected remaster in January 2027). When it launched in 2018, CrossCode received enthusiastic reviews, but it has largely been lost in the shadow of mainstream releases.

articles.title: Marvel TV Boss Says Daredevil: Born Again Was Always Meant to End With Season 3, Despite Previously Suggesting Otherwise
articles.summary: Head of Marvel Television Brad Winderbaum says Daredevil: Born Again was always planned to end with Season 3, despite previously suggesting otherwise. In a new interview with The Brandon Davis Show, Winderbaum was asked about Season 3 being the end of the show.
body: “The plan was always to culminate at 3, because the way we’re looking at it, the original [Netflix] series is 3 seasons, Born Again is 3 seasons. They’re kind of like trade paperbacks or collections that you can slot into your shelves, like these are two 3-volume sets, and then we will take a breath and figure out what’s next for the character.”

Actor Charlie Cox also suggested the same thing at New York Comic-Con, telling GamesRadar that there was a "bit more planning and emotional support" this time. The original Netflix series was unexpectedly and unceremoniously canceled, much to the surprise of the show's writers and cast. However, at some point, the actors were told Born Again would serve as the finale.
Interestingly, Winderbaum told Screen Rant in 2025 that the show was meant to be annualized, with a new season dropping every March.

"That is the plan," said Winderbaum ahead of Season 1 of Born Again. "Season 2 will come out next year, and then hopefully Season 3 and Season Infinity after that. I think this world is extremely rich, and there are many stories to be told on the streets of New York."

articles.title: Epic Is Overhauling Its Anti-Cheat So That Fortnite Can Finally Come To A New Platform
articles.summary: Thanks to devices such as the Steam Deck and Steam Machine, as well as the ongoing issues with Windows, gaming on Linux looks a lot more attractive over the last few years.
body: Epic Games has announced that it is working on a Linux version for Fortnite. It's going to act as a test for Epic's overhaul of EAC (Easy Anti-Cheat), its solution to those developing multiplayer games in Unreal Engine to prevent cheating (most recently used in Gears of War: E-Day). Epic says that it has offered Linux support for its current version of EAC, but that most developers (itself included) opted not to use it and instead omit Linux support entirely because of its inability to be as protective as its Windows version.

A native rebuild of EAC, that doesn't require translation layers such as Proton, would help Epic bring the software up to par with Windows, at which point it would be comfortable finally releasing a native Linux version of Fortnite. In a blog post, Epic says that once it has reached this stage, it will make this available to other developers, too.

"We are also planning to pilot EAC Linux v2 in Fortnite first, where we’ll test it in a live environment and refine it based on what we learn. Once we’ve validated EAC v2’s effectiveness, we’ll make it available to more game developers so they can bring their multiplayer games to Linux players too."

articles.title: Retro Handhelds Loaded With Unlicensed Games Could Face Government Crackdown
articles.summary: The Electronic Software Association (ESA) has a serious bone to pick with retro handhelds that are packaged with tons of unlicensed pre-installed, calling these devices "superfakes" that should face some sort of suppression by the US government.
body: According to an October 6 filing with the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR)--which monitors marketplaces that are accused of engaging in or enabling piracy and counterfeiting--the ESA is urging the government to clamp down on what it calls "illicit plug-and-play consoles and handheld devices." The ESA wants the USTR to add these emulation devices to the Notorious Markets List, the agency's annual report identifying which markets are participating in such behavior, thereby barring or slowing their profits.

"In the video game sector, illicit plug-and-play consoles and handheld devices are the functional equivalent of superfakes," the ESA told the USTR. "They can look and feel like legitimate, mass-market consumer electronics: molded housings, color displays, polished user interfaces, retail packaging, product reviews, warranty-like representations, and listings on familiar e-commerce platforms. Yet their commercial appeal rests solely on a concealed memory card or internal drive loaded with hundreds, thousands, or even tens of thousands of unauthorized copies of copyright-protected games."

articles.title: Total War Fans Blast New Remaster Over Bugs, AI Accusations
articles.summary: Sega and Creative Assembly's new release of Total War: Shogun 2 promised strategy fans an "updated, enhanced, and complete version of the grand strategy classic." But fans of the Total War franchise are ripping the so-called Complete Edition rerelease of Shogun 2 on Steam over bugs and accusations…
body: One day after Total War: Shogun 2 - Complete Edition 's release on Steam, the game carries an "Overwhelmingly Negative" review consensus, with 83% of user reviews skewing negatively.

"Awful, [Creative Assembly], just awful," reads one top-rated user review of Total War: Shogun 2 - Complete Edition on Steam. "So many bugs have not even been addressed, and on top of that you introduce new ones." That reviewer, who has logged 3,507 hours on the original Total War: Shogun 2 on Steam, outlined a series of old, unaddressed bugs, as well as new ones, including poor "ninja balancing."

"Literally the greed they talk about in the Bible," reads another scathing user review. "The whole point of the community wanting these 'old' games ported to 64-bit is better stability and performance, which this game fails miserably at. Instead, they gutted the game of Steam Workshop support and it runs noticeably worse than other modern titles (3K and WH3). They delisted the original game and repackaged it as a new 'Complete Edition' at a higher price. Absolutely shameful."
points: Sega and Creative Assembly's new release of Total War: Shogun 2 promised strategy fans an "updated, enhanced, and complete version of the grand strategy classic.

articles.title: 3 months after launch, Riot announces League of Legends Classic will be killed in January: 'most have gone back to other parts of League'
articles.summary: League of Legends Classic was Riot's attempt to capitalise on nostalgia for vintage-era LoL. It stripped away most of the champions and kits introduced since 2013, reverted to an older version of the Summoner's Rift map, and promised to roll out "new" old Champions at a faster clip than in the…
body: But the nostalgia Riot must have hoped would sustain the mode hasn't proven sufficient enough to keep it running: the mode will go offline in January 2027, only six months after its launch.
"We’ve seen a lot of players have fun revisiting the olden days with Classic," a Riot spokesperson wrote in a new update. "At this point though, most have gone back to other parts of League."
As a result, the current season will be the last. "We’ll then put Classic back in the box for now, with the goal of bringing it back, likely as an event mode with adjustments and additions."

It continues: "There’s more we’re going to share in the future about what we learned from this run. That includes where we think we got Classic right, where we could have gone more classic, and where sticking too closely to the past may have held the experience back."

articles.title: State lawsuits accuse OpenAI of ignoring its own safety warnings for profit: 'All these harms were foreseeable and avoidable'
articles.summary: The attorney generals for eight US states announced today that they are suing OpenAI. West Virginia, Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, Arkansas, Arizona, Idaho, and Montana have all filed lawsuits alleging that the ChatGPT maker has deceived and endangered the public, particularly children, in the name of…
body: The complaints allege that ChatGPT has "coached" users to harm themselves and others, and—quoting the West Virginia filing specifically—state that "there is a growing body of research indicating that ChatGPT is also degrading critical thinking skills, encouraging paranoias and delusions, offering dangerous medical advice, and promoting unhealthy behaviors and relationships."
Recent tales of "rogue" AI agents are also presented by as evidence of recklessness.

"All these harms were foreseeable and avoidable," reads the West Virginia complaint [ PDF ]. "[OpenAI CEO Sam Altman] himself has warned about the safety risks of AI since at least 2015. It is no secret that children use ChatGPT. And numerous OpenAI employees have left over safety concerns."

OpenAI acknowledged last year that its systems can "fall short" when responding to users in distress, but said that it has "a stack of layered safeguards" in place to help. The company also says on its website that it now uses "age prediction" to place some users in a teen-oriented ChatGPT experience with "additional safeguards," unless they verify that they are adults.
points: The attorney generals for eight US states announced today that they are suing OpenAI.

We know many of you can’t wait to get your hands on the next METRO, and are in desperate need of a wearable Spartan Helmet replica to add to your gaming collection.
We recently revealed that Blueprints are a new feature in METRO 2039, encouraging exploration and allowing you to craft upgrades and attachments for weapons and gear.
The Specialist Pack pre-order bonus, available for all pre-ordered editions, gives you the opportunity to unlock these early.
